page: Vultr vhp-4c-8gb-amd is a shared-CPU virtual machine belonging to the High Performance server family. It is configured with an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor offering 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 180 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark data indicates that the shared CPU allocation and memory architecture present performance tradeoffs. Stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests show average performance, with scores of 2306.16 and 9232.12 respectively. However, memory bandwidth for large, potentially uncached blocks is poor, measuring 17.9 GB/sec for reads and 12.56 GB/sec for writes. Geekbench scores also reflect these constraints, with a single-core score of 877.0 and a multi-core score of 2823.0. Cryptographic performance is a relative strength, with the Passmark CPU encryption test achieving an average rating.

Given its shared CPU architecture and modest memory-to-core ratio, this server type offers a cost-efficient entry point for workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated CPU performance. It is suited for lightweight applications such as basic web serving, software compilation tasks, small-scale database operations, and low-concurrency background processing.
